newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Compaq busy as stock bucks trend.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Compaq busy as stock bucks trend.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp options were fairly busy Thursday, with the bulk of activity put selling, as the stock went against the broad market grain to trade sharply lower, traders said.

In afternoon action, Compaq was down 2-3/8 at 97-1/2 on more than 4.8 million shares even as the rest of the stock market rallied. The bellwether Dow industrial average .DJI was up 123 points, or 1.6 percent, at 7,698.

Some traders said Compaq was being sold off after circuit maker Integrated Device Technology said late Wednesday its fiscal first quarter earnings would fall short of expectations mainly because of weaker-than-expected demand in its PC-related business segments.
"We've had a lot of put sellers," a market maker in Compaq options said. "There's always a new seller stepping up in the stock."
Among the Compaq options, the June 100 put was most active, with turnover of nearly 3,300 contracts. The July 90 put traded roughly 3,210.
The busiest Compaq puts included the June 100, with volume of about 2,440 contracts and the June 105 with volume of 1,890.
On Wednesday, Compaq said contrary to market rumors, it had no plans to forecast its second quarter earnings. A spokeswoman added that, "Business is good."
Traders said investor worry about second quarter earnings at technology companies has been especially high since Intel Corp said its second quarter profits would fall short of expectations.
Intel also fell Thursday, losing 3-3/4 to 143-3/4.

The market maker said volatility in Compaq options has been steadily increasing over the last couple of weeks and that in the July series had reached around 50. Its historical volatility is around 40.
He added that volatility in the July options was higher than in the other months.
Options on shares of Integrated Device were fairly busy and volatility maintained a firm bias even after being driven up ahead of the company's earnings announcement Wednesday, traders said.
"You're starting to see some sellers of premium, but not excessive," one trader at the Chicago Board Options Exchange said, referring to Integrated Device options.
He said most of the action was from one investor unwinding a put position opened Wednesday as the stock fell.
At the CBOE, the Integrated Device June 12-1/2 put traded 1,295 contracts by late trade.
"That's been the largest single block," he said. "The rest is just normal order flow.
"A lot of different firms are doing a little of everything. Nothing predominant," he added.
